I completely hate with how little respect players are treated that bought a full price game. I understand that releasing a game always surfaces bugs that need fixing and while even that was something game studios had figured out to prevent in the CD era of games (!) I am mostly OK with it. But how careless do you have to be to NOT make sure savegames load even if your servers have issues. I don't want to sit here waiting for some poor dev to churn out production hot fixes on a friday afternoon to be able to load a save game THAT SITS ON MY DISK! The stuff studios are fine with shipping these days absolutely amazes me in the most disappointing way.
Still an Alpha game. Basic Graphics settings don't even work correctly. DLSS is choppy and HDR is terrible. Super bad edge highlights while moving with HDR on. Tested on 2 Higher end PCS

Very Buggy game, my deluxe content is not available in game, many species just are not available in the trading center in franchise mode. I have over 200 hours in PZ1 and was very excited for this game, pre ordered it, watched all the trailers etc. but the actual game is just a disappointment, half the world has no species, and it is just so obvious this game is just a framework to extract money from the players via DLCs that have content that should've been in the base game. Performance is also bad. 40 fps 1080p high

Probably the most disappointing release in a long time.

The aquariums are buggy as hell. Most of the time, you can't even fill them with water, so you end up with nothing but a glass box. I spent over half an hour refreshing the animal market just to buy an animal, only to end up with a half-dead boar.

You can't unlock new animals because you need a 3-star zoo, which is practically impossible to achieve when it takes half an hour just to buy animals that are already half-dead...

I expected way more, especially considering this is a sequel to basically the same game, with only a few additions.

Guess I'll wait for about 10 patches before the game is actually playable.

Absolutely amazing sequel to an already fantastic zoo management game. The expansion of gameplay into Wildlife Reserves really adds an extra layer of meaning and accomplishment to franchise mode, as well as the accreditation tiers. I am very excited to see what future DLC adds to the game!
I am addicted! The bugs & crashes reverting my progress is annoying but understandable for such a big new game.

This game will become excellent eventually, but it just isn't there yet. It looks beautiful, and there is a clear upgrade on my much loved PZ1 in here somewhere. Unfortunately, the number of bugs is exhausting, the guests are impossible to please and the wildlife reserves are a strange distraction nobody was asking for at launch and for me completely distract from what I want to do, build cool zoos.

I think if Frontier had taken the time they wasted on wildlife reserves and put that into testing and developing the core zoo product, it would have been a much stronger game at launch. Save the reserves for a large DLC or even spin-off game where the mechanics and ecology could have been developed properly.

It's incredibly disappointing, we paid for a full priced game and received an early access experience. I can overlook some bugs, but there are several game breaking bugs that makes playing impossible/very difficult. I was SO excited for this game, and now I barely play it.
after 35 hours of testing all mechanics i fell in love in that game deffinitly can recommend it

I had high expectations and I feel let down.

First thing? Middle of the campaign, I search for a community habitat to become home of my tucsons. Habitat prepetually loads, need to restart game, lose last save.

Bugs? Loads of them, animal behaviour, being constantly boxed or randomly escaping from perfectly secure environments.

Release groups in franchise mode do not work properly.

There is a tremendous lack of "common zoo species".

List goes on.

I really wanted to like this game as someone who grew up loving Zoo Tycoon 2.

The prebuilt zoos in the campaign look great, but starting from scratch quickly becomes frustrating. Building paths and habitat walls without a grid-based system feels unnecessarily tedious. The game seems to prioritize deep customization at the expense of the actual fun parts of managing a zoo. I appreciate the creative freedom, but I wish it were easier to focus on the bigger picture rather than constantly struggling with the basic building tools.
I do like it but You're basically running a wildlife breeding programme at the speed of continental drift.

Why not release this game in Early Access and price it accordingly? Charging ¥8,000 for what feels like a beta test is ridiculous. Franchise mode is riddled with bugs, and there’s no excuse for releasing the game in this state.
I originally planned to wait a few weeks for patches to address the launch-day issues before leaving a review. Instead, I’m posting now as a warning to others: don’t spend ¥8,000 on this until it’s in a condition that actually justifies a full-price release.
Customers shouldn’t be paying full price to do your quality assurance. At this point, you should be paying me to test your game—not the other way around.
I will update this review in a few weeks to see if they have addressed the issues. In the meantime I am going to write to your customer services team as I feel like I have not received the product that I paid my hard earned money for.
This is my first time playing a game of this type and I am addicted!!

It's a very engaging game, even in its current buggy state. I know you're working on fixing things, but you should have hired testers for this. Paying players shouldn't be expected to help fix your game.

One important issue that isn't a bug: players shouldn't be allowed to resell animals they previously purchased at the market (not for special credits at least). Some players buy animals solely to resell them at ridiculous prices.
Game has obvious bugs that need repairing but the team at PZ2 are working hard to fix and correct any issues. The game is very much improved from PZ1 and i cant wait to see more in the future.

I've never played a game with this many bugs before, and it's been really disappointing. I've encountered so many different issues, some just annoying but then I had a game breaking bug in career mode that left me unable to progress. I even tried to get a refund but by the time I reached that point I was already past Steam's 2 hours of gameplay refund window.. I've since read that my specific issue may have been fixed in an update which I'm glad to hear, but I'm still disappointed with the overall state of the game at release. I understand that bugs happen and I don't expect any game to be perfect. I just wish there had been more talk about the issues before release. It's just so frustrating to look forward to a game like this and pay full price and then not be able to play it properly. I really hope the game continues to improve because I do want to enjoy it. I just think it's reasonable to expect a more reliable experience at launch especially for a full priced game. For now, I'd recommend waiting awhile for more updates or a big sale before buying it.

Are there bugs? Absolutely! And there are things that need to be improved as well, but other than that, it's a step forward compared to PZ1. Also a lot of fun new animals. And the fact that there will be DLCs again shouldn't come as a surprise to most people either, because that's simply how the gaming industry works nowadays, and it's up to the user whether they want that or not. The price of the base game is not too much at all, and you get a complete game for it.

I'll start with the good. The core of the game is fun. Zoo's are beautiful, animals are cool to watch. The management part is okay from what I've played so far.

Now, the bad, which is a lot because this game is so buggy and broken. People say the game isn't unplayable because it's just bugs, but it's not true. 

In franchise mode: I've had to delete an entire zoo because after doing some pathing adjustments, animals were randomly escaping from habitats that were unchanged and stood firm for ages. I have a zoo that constantly turns the entire power off and I have to reboot to the game to fix it.

In career mode: I have a bugged bird enclosure that just randomly sets birds free.

I'll also say that pathing is very powerful, but unless you're really good at it, you will spend so much time preventing it just looking ugly and misaligned. It's so uninituitive. There need to be better in-game tutorials for that.

Lastly, it's a shame they reduced the accreditation requirements, because this was the part of the game that gave you challenges and goals, now they've updated it to be way too easy.

I am putting this game on hold because I've ended up wasting so much time due to basic functionality not working properly.
Unfortunately it seems Frontier did no QA testing at all, there are SO MANY BUGS (DLSS doesn’t even work). Shame on them for using us as unpaid beta testers, I refunded

I have been really excited to play this, seeing all the new additions. The concept still remains a great, fun game. However, it's current state is one where I would say it should have been released as early access. I had seen so many reports of this game being full of bugs and I hadn't encountered anything by that point, but now I'm seeing the bugs and getting the random crashes, losing loads of progress. Frontier, although they are releasing updates, don't seem to be addressing a lot of the issues, which is a real shame. I hope they start to introduce some real fixes as it feels like they have been lazy with it. I wouldn't get this game just yet, wait a few months for the fixes, I wish I did.

Can't recommend in its current state. I love Frontier and their games. I know they will fix all the issues eventually, but I didn't expect it to be this broken at launch. There are game breaking bugs throughout. Animals escape from pens constantly then get boxed up and left in other pens forever. Staff are not responding to issues correctly. Some shops and facilities are inaccessible by guests or staff. The list goes on. These bugs prevent progression in Career mode and make any other mode very frustrating to play. 

At the time of this writing, Frontier has released one patch and has promised another by the end of the week. I have no doubt they will fix all of the issues, I just wish they had spent a little more time on playtesting or a short early access period. 

In my opinion, the game itself (if one looks beyond the bugs) is fantastic. The pathing is leaps and bounds above the first game. The wildlife reserves, aquariums, and aviaries are really cool. I love the new theming and all the new parts. It's going to be a great game once it's fixed.
Seriously, no population management for exhibits? I just want to refund this and never look back.

This game had some bugs when it come out, and it was still playable for me, although frustrating. That said the last couple weeks have had some great updates that have fixed the issues I was having. 
IF you played the first game and liked it, this definitely has some huge quality of life improvements (hello, improved pathing). There is a lot to do, a lot to manage. That is what makes it fun for me, but if you don't like that, you could try this on sandbox with some settings tweaked, or skip it. I love it though!

This game needs a lot of help. Some of the new features are nice, but I find my game crashing every few hours. I also spent three hours trying to build a pond, and the aquarium pieces don't work well at all.
If you're trying to create anything natural with animals, like what they've advertised, don't bother. Installing the gate and dealing with all the frustration that comes with it just isn't worth it.
I honestly don't understand how koi ponds are even supposed to work or how to build them. I tried following the tutorial and spent hours on it, only to walk away having learned absolutely nothing. The whole experience is frustrating and needs serious improvement. On top of that, there are barely any animals available, and there's no promise that DLC from the previous game will carry over. It honestly feels like a Sims betrayal, but somehow worse. It reminds me of ARK, where it feels like you're getting another version of the same game without enough meaningful differences to justify starting over.
I spent a lot of money on DLC for the previous game, so it's incredibly frustrating to feel like that investment doesn't mean much anymore. After all the money and time I've put into the first game, I have very little motivation to spend even more on DLC for the second one. Right now, the game feels like a step backward rather than an exciting new experience.

I love the game, maybe more as a concept than as an executed project. it has incredible potential. I just do not understand how it was released after a demo version where loads of errors were flagged (and none addressed at the time) and for that price tag, which is justified because this is a massive project but as a consumer, it is quite discouraging when you encounter glitch after glitch, and quite common ones. there are not only code issues, but also structural issues to the story that make your life way too difficult (I know this has been addressed by the developers, but still worth mentioning because it remains not optimal). the first few hours went smooth: however, the more you advance in the campaign, the more (very frustrating) glitches and problems I encountered. I didn't even try to make a franchise yet, very happy about that. can't imagine how frustrating it'd been to build a thing of my own when everyone else's zoos were already crappy! after all that built-up frustration (this game is supposed to be challenging but fun, in my opinion), the game fully crashed. that was sad. I really hope the game will rapidly improve. the momentum is very much lost, though.
